title: Optimizing High Flow Nasal Cannula Oxygenation in Pediatric Airway Procedures
official: Optimizing High Flow Nasal Cannula Oxygenation in Pediatric Airway Procedures: a Randomized Study
summary: The purpose of this study is to investigate which flow rate (higher versus lower) is most effective at increasing apneic time and preventing greater than 5% drop in desaturation, as well as assessing transcutaneous carbon dioxide (CO2) levels during airway procedures in children
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* undergoing laryngoscopy and bronchoscopy procedures at Children's Memorial Hermann Hospital (CMHH)
* weight greater than or equal to 5 kilograms and using flow rates between 5 to 45 liters per minute (BTPS)

Exclusion Criteria:

* Emergency type cases, tracheostomy patients, unrepaired cyanotic heart disease, nasal deformity/choanal atresia, or cautery/laser type procedures
sponsor: The University of Texas Health Science Center, Houston

sites.f: The University of Texas Health Science Center at Houston
